focus.text:
(1) An applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a passport in her/his new name. See 8 FAM 1001.5 regarding applying for a replacement passport in a new name;

(2) An applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a form FS-240 in her/his new name. See 8 FAM 1001.3 regarding amending a form FS-240; and

(3) You must clear the applicant's pending name even though the name change is not final and even if the passport is not being issued at this time.

d. The court order or decree must list both the applicant's current and former name(s).

EXCEPTION: You may receive a court order in which the applicant's former name is made confidential (e.g., California's Safe at Home program). When this occurs, the applicant must provide both her/his current and former names on the application. You may request additional evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or identity in accordance with 22 CFR 51.23 and 22 CFR 51.45.

8 FAM 403.1-3(B) Name Spacing

(CT:CITZ-96; 08-04-2023)

a. In accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) recommendations, U.S. passports, form FS-240, and form DS-2060 are printed in all uppercase letters. Printing a name with multiple parts in uppercase letters causes the name to appear as one word unless the parts are separated with spaces. Consequently, if the applicant has a name with multiple parts, you must determine how the name will appear:

(1) If the applicant's previous passport had a space, you should add a space on the current application;

(2) If the applicant does not have a previous passport and the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or ID has a space, you should add a space on the current application; or

(3) If the applicant expresses a clear preference to add or remove space, either verbally or in writing, you may add or remove it per the applicant's preference.

NOTE: If you receive applications from several family members, you should space the last names consistently, unless a family member expresses a clear preference for a different spacing.

NOTE: For special-issuance passports, the spacing of an eligible family member's last name should match the spacing of the last name of the sponsor.

b. Name spacing issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport, unless the Department disregarded the applicant's clear preference (see 8 FAM 1001.2).

c. Arabic ordinal numbers must be changed to Roman numerals, for example, 2nd to II, 3rd to III:

d. Some applicants may include the prefix “Sr.” as an abbreviation for “Señor” in Spanish meaning “Mr.” or “Mister” in English. If you determine that this is the case, follow the guidance in 8 FAM 403.1-5(C) regarding ranks and titles.

e. Name suffix issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport, unless the Department disregarded the applicant's clear preference (see 8 FAM 1001.2).
